newsitem.title: UK: National Grid helped by FT's Lex comment.
newsitem.headline: National Grid helped by FT's Lex comment.

text.p: Shares in the National Grid rose to a twelve-month high on Wednesday following upbeat comments in the influential Financial Times Lex column.
The shares were up 6-1/2p at 213p by 0952 GMT, after gaining 27 percent in the last six months.
The Financial Times said a victory in the election by the opposition Labour Party had been overdiscounted by water and electricity stocks.
The Labour Party has promised to impose a windfall tax on utility profits if it comes to power and Labour is currently running around 20 points ahead in opinion polls.
The FT noted that in picking potential outperformers among the sector it would be best to go for the "sleepiest businesses," adding that National Grid was currently "undermanaged."
One leading industry analyst said he remained positive on the shares up to 245p.
"We've been positive on the generators since October," he said. "And we're very positive on National Grid because it has the best chance in the sector of avoiding any windfall tax."
